subject.title: [security] Public artifact URLs disclose authenticated owner and organization identities

question: Which stable secret and compatibility policy should define non-reversible organization and owner segments for future artifact grants while preserving existing v2 URLs?
rationale: Source inspection establishes the unnecessary disclosure, but automation should not invent the cryptographic key-lifecycle contract or the persisted URL compatibility promise.

options.title: Add v3 keyed pseudonyms
options.body: Derive domain-separated organization and owner pseudonyms from an existing stable deployment secret for new grants while leaving all v2 URLs valid.

options.title: Add a dedicated namespace secret
options.body: Introduce a separately configured and versioned artifact-namespace secret with explicit setup, restoration, and rotation documentation.

options.title: Accept and document disclosure
options.body: Retain reversible v2 identities and explicitly document that artifact URLs expose exact authenticated organization and owner metadata.

recommendation.title: Add v3 keyed pseudonyms
recommendation.body: Derive domain-separated organization and owner pseudonyms from an existing stable deployment secret for new grants while leaving all v2 URLs valid.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current v2 namespace and its compatibility policy, making them the strongest available owner for the next namespace contract.
